**ABOUT PUBLIC COUNSEL**

Public Counsel is a nonprofit public interest law firm dedicated to advancing civil rights and racial and economic justice, as well as to amplifying the power of our clients through comprehensive legal advocacy. Founded on and strengthened by a pro bono legal service model, our staff and volunteers seek justice through direct legal services, promote healthy and resilient communities through education and outreach, and support community-led efforts to transform unjust systems through litigation and policy advocacy in and beyond Los Angeles.

Public Counsel organizes its work through seven legal teams: Child, Youth & Family Advocacy, Community Development, Consumer Rights & Economic Justice, Homelessness Prevention, Immigrants’ Rights, Education Equity, and our impact litigation team, Opportunity Under Law.

Public Counsel has a staff of approximately 170. We are committed to building a diverse staff and encourage applications from people of color, people with disabilities, and people of all gender identities, gender expressions, and sexualities. We recognize the essential role of staff in achieving our goals, and we have set a long-term intention to provide competitive compensation, benefits, training, mentorship, and overall workplace wellness, making Public Counsel a leader among nonprofit law firms.

**POSITION OVERVIEW**

Reporting to the Vice President, Chief Advocacy Officer, the Director of Policy & Coalition Building provides strategic leadership for Public Counsel’s policy advocacy and coalition-building efforts across the organization. The Director works closely with program leaders and staff to identify policy priorities, strengthen coordination of existing policy work, and develop systems that enable Public Counsel to leverage its expertise and resources effectively. The Director builds and maintains relationships with community organizations, coalitions, policymakers, and other partners; provides guidance and technical assistance on policy advocacy; and helps connect policy work with Public Counsel’s direct services and impact litigation efforts. The Director also works collaboratively with the Directors of Litigation and Pro Bono, the Communications and Development teams, and other organizational leaders to advance Public Counsel’s policy goals and visibility. The ideal candidate is a strategic, collaborative, and highly organized leader who brings strong policy expertise, relationship-building skills, and a commitment to client- and community-centered advocacy.

**ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES**

_**Strategic Policy Leadership & Internal Organization**_

- Develop and advance a coordinated organizational approach to policy advocacy that supports Public Counsel’s mission, advances systems change, and amplifies the expertise of legal teams and staff
- Assess and organize Public Counsel’s existing policy work, identify opportunities for coordination and joint advocacy, and establish systems for tracking, sharing, and reporting policy activity and outcomes
- Work with legal team leaders and staff to identify policy priorities and develop strategies that leverage Public Counsel’s expertise and resources
- Develop and maintain internal guidelines, tools, and resources for policy advocacy, including processes for developing organizational positions and addressing compliance, lobbying, and disclosure requirements
- Convene and facilitate cross-team policy working groups and other fora to promote information-sharing, collaboration, and coordinated advocacy
- Advise organizational leadership and staff on policy strategy, including how policy advocacy can complement and strengthen direct services and strategic litigation

_**Coalition, Community & Government Relations**_

- Build and maintain strong relationships with grassroots organizations, community leaders, coalition partners, policymakers, government officials and staff
- Advance a community-centered model of coalition building and advocacy that supports community-led policy initiatives and incorporates partner priorities into Public Counsel’s policy strategies
- Identify and cultivate opportunities for Public Counsel to participate in, lead, or support coalitions and policy campaigns consistent with organizational priorities
- Provide guidance and support to Public Counsel staff in developing and maintaining external policy relationships and navigating political and coalition dynamics
- Represent Public Counsel’s policy priorities with policymakers, coalition partners, community organizations, funders, media, and other external audiences
- Build relationships with pro bono, academic, and other partners to bring additional expertise and capacity to Public Counsel’s policy advocacy

_**Policy Development, Advocacy & Analysis**_

- Provide technical assistance to staff in identifying policy opportunities, developing policy proposals, and crafting legislative and administrative advocacy strategies
- Monitor and analyze relevant federal, state, and local legislation, regulations, and policy developments and help assess their implications for Public Counsel’s clients, communities, and policy priorities
- Support the development of legislation, policy proposals, comment letters, testimony, public comments, policy briefs, and other advocacy materials
- Work with staff and coalition partners to develop and advance policy campaigns, including strategies for legislative, administrative, and other policy advocacy
- Help ensure that Public Counsel’s policy positions are coordinated, consistent with organizational priorities, and informed by client and community perspectives
- Partner with the Communications team to translate complex policy issues into clear, accessible messages and elevate the visibility and impact of Public Counsel’s policy advocacy

_**Organizational Capacity Building & External Engagement**_

- Identify policy-related training and capacity-building needs across the organization and develop or facilitate training, mentorship, and other resources to strengthen staff policy advocacy skills
- Develop and improve systems, tools, and processes that make policy advocacy more efficient, coordinated, and accessible to staff across Public Counsel
- Work with organizational leadership and the Development team to identify funding opportunities and strengthen grants and other support for policy advocacy and coalition-building efforts
- Collaborates  with the Communications, Development, and other organizational teams to advance Public Counsel’s policy priorities and external visibility
- Represent Public Counsel at conferences, panels, community forums, meetings with elected officials, and other public and professional settings
- Contribute to organizational leadership and agency-wide initiatives, including efforts to advance equity, inclusion, racial and economic justice, and community-centered advocacy

Requirements

**ESSENTIAL JOB SKILLS AND ABILITIES**

- Bachelor’s degree, with an advanced degree in public policy, law, public administration, communications, or a related field preferred
- At least 10 years of progressively responsible experience in policy advocacy, legislative affairs, government relations, coalition building, public affairs, community organizing, or a related field, with substantial experience leading policy initiatives
- Significant experience navigating legislative and/or policy processes at the federal, state, or local level, with experience working across multiple levels of government strongly preferred
- Demonstrated experience developing, advancing, or leading legislation, policy campaigns, regulatory advocacy, or other significant policy initiatives
- Significant experience working collaboratively with and developing and maintaining strong, trusting relationships with community organizations, grassroots advocates, coalitions, elected officials, legislative staff, and other external stakeholders
- Strong organizational and project-management skills, including the ability to develop systems, establish priorities, track multiple projects and deadlines, coordinate complex work across teams
- Inspiring, collaborative, transparent, inclusive, and approachable leadership style
- Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex legal, technical, or policy issues into clear and accessible messages for different audiences, including in collaboration with communications teams
- Demonstrated ability to assess an organization’s existing policy work, identify gaps and opportunities, and develop practical systems and strategies to improve coordination and effectiveness
- Strong strategic judgment and the ability to distinguish among opportunities that Public Counsel should lead, support, monitor, or decline to pursue
- Strong meeting facilitation, consensus-building, diplomacy, and conflict-management skills
- Demonstrated ability to work cooperatively across teams, levels, and functions within an organization and to build trust among colleagues with different levels of experience and expertise, including by providing thoughtful technical assistance and mentorship to colleagues with varying levels of familiarity with policy advocacy
- Demonstrated commitment to racial and economic justice, and advancing diversity, equity, and inclusion in the workplace and in the communities Public Counsel serves
- High levels of emotional intelligence and cultural competency, including being curious, self-aware, cognizant of bias, compassionate, patient, and willing to listen, and having a growth mindset and openness to new perspectives
- Spanish-language proficiency is a plus

**JOB TYPE AND BENEFITS**

- Full-time/exempt
- Salary range is $135,000–$165,000, with most candidates expected to fall within the middle of the range, depending on experience
- Non-bargaining

**Public Counsel offers a competitive benefits package including**:

- Medical coverage with an option for 100% employer-paid employee and dependent child(ren)’s premiums; buy-up options are available for other HMO and PPO coverage
- Dental and vision coverage
- Option to enroll in a Flexible Spending Account
- Employer-paid life insurance and disability plans

**Generous paid time off (per year):**

- 15 accrued vacation days that increase to 20 days after 3 years of employment
- 12 accrued sick days that may be used for physical and mental health needs
- 2 personal observance days
- 11 paid holidays plus 2 one-week office closures (during the summer and winter)
- Up to 60 hours of compensatory time per calendar year (for exempt staff only)

**Additional benefits:**

- 403(b) retirement plan with an elective employee contribution, and after a year of employment a discretionary employer contribution
- Free on-site parking or public transportation reimbursement
- $45 per pay period for employees who use non-English language skills to perform work duties
- Up to 6 months of parental leave
- Organizational and team wellness activities to build team cohesion and camaraderie
- Professional development support and opportunities
- Annual payment of dues for required licenses or certifications (state bar dues for attorneys) and for a mutually agreed-upon professional organization
- Centrally located headquarters in the heart of Koreatown, a vibrant neighborhood with easy access to public transportation, diverse dining options, and cultural attractions

**HOW TO APPLY**

We value lived experiences and experiences working with clients across a range of settings. Please discuss such experiences in your cover letter, especially if they are not reflected in your resume. We strongly encourage interested candidates to apply no later than **November 30, 2026.** We plan to start interviewing candidates during the week of January 11, 2027. Please submit the following materials:

If you are unable to submit any one of these materials through our portal linked below, please email it to Erica Garcia at egarcia@publiccounsel.org with the subject line: DPCB Application Supplement.

title: Product Analyst Level I
description:
About the Role

OnPath is MedRisk’s intelligent bill routing and network optimization solution for workers’ compensation medical bill review. This role takes ownership of the recurring analytical and enablement work so product leaders can focus on strategy and delivery.

A client asks a question. You work out what they are really asking, write it up so our data team can act on it, check what comes back, and turn it into something the client can use. You own the timeline and chase the open items across internal teams and outside partners until the work is finished.

This is an analytical role with a client-facing edge. You will spend real time on the data and also sit on client calls to present findings and answer questions on the spot, working to priorities set by Product Management. It suits someone who knows when a number needs a second look, can explain how they got there without jargon, and stays with a problem until it is closed. Excel is the analytical tool for the job.

What You Will Do

Client engagement and requirements

  • Work with clients, account teams and service delivery to understand the business question behind a request, rather than just the data being asked for
  • Join client calls to walk through findings, answer questions live, and take requirements directly from the client
  • Translate that question into a written request for the data team, covering scope, population, states, date range, metric definitions and output format
  • Answer the data team’s follow-up questions and track requests through to delivery against client commitments
  • Capture decisions and action items from enhancement and design sessions, and write them up as requirements the delivery teams can work from

Analysis and quality assurance

  • Analyze returned data to answer questions on routing performance, network savings, reduction rates and reconsideration activity
  • Check each analysis before it goes out. Reconcile the totals, confirm the savings categorization and the state and network logic, and make sure it answers the question that was asked
  • Flag outliers and gaps with supporting detail, and follow variances until the cause is understood

Client reporting and deliverables

  • Build and maintain recurring client deliverables in Excel and PowerPoint, including network mosaic comparisons, savings and reconsideration reporting, projection versus actuals, and account status decks
  • Quantify and report savings generated by OnPath routing, with trending analysis and recommendations
  • Translate routing, repricing and cascade logic into plain language that account teams and clients can act on

Project management and follow-through

  • Own delivery timelines for client requests and product workstreams, and hold them against competing priorities
  • Coordinate across data, analytics, operations, compliance and account teams to keep multi-party deliverables moving
  • Maintain the request and open item trackers, with owners and due dates, covering internal work as well as outstanding deliverables and defects with routing partners
  • Produce the recurring status reporting that keeps clients and internal teams aligned, and follow up on each open item until it closes
  • Log production issues, stay with them through triage, and keep the affected teams posted

Product enablement and training

  • Maintain content for the client-facing dashboard, including page descriptions, FAQs and access coordination
  • Author and maintain methodology documentation, configuration references and release notes
  • Train internal teams on how OnPath routing works, what the outputs mean, and how to read the client-facing dashboard
  • Build and maintain training material, job aids and internal FAQs, and onboard new account and client-facing team members to the product
  • Act as a day-to-day resource for account teams, service delivery managers and internal partners with questions about OnPath results

Sales and prospect support

  • Support requests for proposal and prospect analysis with network and savings summaries, use cases and one-pagers

What You Bring

Required

  • An analytical background, with three to five years in an analyst, business analyst or reporting role, ideally in healthcare, insurance, managed care or claims
  • Advanced Excel, including pivot tables, lookups and reconciling data from more than one source, plus strong PowerPoint and Word
  • Ability to turn a loosely worded business question into a clear request someone else can execute, and to review the finished analysis for accuracy and reasonableness
  • Accurate with financial and operational data, and inclined to reconcile a figure before publishing it
  • Clear communication, including presenting findings to clients and explaining methodology to people who do not work with data
  • Able to hold a timeline, coordinate people who do not report to you, and chase open items until they are closed

Preferred

  • Workers’ compensation medical bill review, PPO network, or payment integrity background
  • Familiarity with provider data concepts including TIN, NPI, CPT, state fee schedules and participating versus non-participating logic
  • Experience viewing or maintaining reports in Power BI or a similar tool
  • Jira or a comparable work management tool
  • Experience in a client-facing role such as client success, account management or service delivery
  • Exposure to vendor or partner coordination

What Success Looks Like in the First Year

  • Requests reach the data team complete and unambiguous, and come back needing fewer rounds of rework
  • Recurring client reporting is delivered on a predictable cadence and is accurate on first pass
  • Able to walk a client through the reporting unaided, explain what changed when a report is updated or modified and why, and answer the follow-up questions without escalating
  • Product documentation and dashboard content stay current without prompting
  • Open items close on schedule, and clients are not left waiting on follow-up
  • The product team spends measurably more time on roadmap work and less on support and stabilization

Additional Information

This position sits within Product Management. Travel is minimal.

Compensation: $90,000 to $110,000 annually, depending on experience and location.

title: Chief Engineer, DCEO, Data Center Engineering Operations
description:
Job Description

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

AWS is looking for a detail-oriented individual to join our Data Center Engineering Operations (DCEO) Team. This committed group works to maintain the critical physical infrastructure that supports Amazon Web Services. Specifically, this team works to ensure that the data center's MEP operates at 100% availability while maintaining first-class customer service to the teams and groups within the data centers.

As the Data Center Engineering Operation (DCEO) Chief Engineer (CE), you will be responsible for ensuring that all electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment within the data center is operating at peak efficiency. This involves both planned preventative maintenance of equipment, daily corrective work, and emergency response to emergent issues. You will serves as an expert technical resource reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager and interacting with onsite Engineering Operations Technicians (EOT) and any third party vendors. Being the singular focal point for all facility operations within a given data center, you will support Amazon within its owned and operated data centers. Data center equipment that supports mission-critical servers must maintain better than 99.999% uptime.

As the DCEO Chief Engineer you will manage small-to-medium impacting projects from conception to completion. These projects involve large amounts of independent work as well as collaboration with external support groups including engineering, automation, processing, and finance in both local and global settings. Creating and delivering on key milestones, obtaining and tracking quotes for all necessary costs, and documenting project results for future implementation at other facilities. The goals of such projects are for the CE to drive innovation and resiliency while reducing operational costs in the facilities.

One of the best parts to this role is that you will direct, train and support Engineering Operation Technicians in their role of providing hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting and operations. Implementation and execution of site/equipment-specific training exercises is also expected. This equipment includes, but is not limited to, stand-by diesel generators, switchgear, UPS’s, PDU’s, AHU’s, chillers, cooling towers, chemical treatment systems, pumps, motors, VFD’s, and building automation systems.

Key job responsibilities
• Oversee the day-to-day operations and maintenance of mechanical and electrical equipment in a data center.
• Operate independently with limited direct management
• Act as an escalation point for all facilities-related issues within the data center, escalating to the Data Center Facility Manager as needed
• Perform root cause analysis of equipment failures
• Troubleshoot and report of facility and data sever-level events within internal SLA
• Create and deploy new standard practices for Engineering Operations Technicians, Chief Engineers, and vendor support teams
• Provide training and guidance to Engineering Operations Technicians
• Ensure all safety procedures are adhered to by vendor and Amazon staff
• Utilize internal CMMS to manage building workflows
• Communicate complex technical information to a non-technical audience

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. title: Carlin - Senior Geologic Modeler
description:
Description

Are you a Geology professional who is looking for career growth? Nevada Gold Mines' (NGM) Mineral Resource Management team has the perfect opportunity for you!

At Nevada Gold Mines, the Geologic Modeler is a technical role responsible for developing, maintaining, and advancing fit-for-purpose geological models that directly support resource growth, mine planning, and operational excellence. This role leads the implementation of best-practice 3D geological modeling workflows by integrating geological, geophysical, and geochemical data with field observations to deliver high-quality, defensible interpretations.

You will work closely with mine and resource geologists, engineers, operations, and data scientists to ensure geological models meet business needs, industry standards, and operational timelines—while continuously improving how we model and understand our orebodies.

Responsibilities

  • Lead and promote Nevada Gold Mines’ Journey to Zero safety culture and company values with an emphasis in visible felt leadership and time in the field
  • Deliver high-priority geological model updates on schedule to support business needs.
  • Conduct regular field visits to mentor teams and validate geological models.
  • Ensure compliance with role responsibilities, annual deliverables, and company standards.
  • Communicate progress, risks, and opportunities to key stakeholders.
  • Work closely with Mine and Resource Geologists to set modeling priorities aligned with operational requirements.
  • Collaborate with engineering and operations teams to support short- and long-term mine planning, maximizing ore recovery and minimizing dilution.
  • Support grade control, orebody knowledge transfer, and optimization of mill feed quality.
  • Integrate drilling, mapping, and reconciliation data to improve model accuracy and performance.
  • Support optimization of the 5-year mine plan and communicate geological risks and opportunities.
  • Assist the Geology Superintendent as needed and support model validation across the geology value chain.
  • Follow all HS&E policies and procedures, identify and mitigate risks, and promote safe work practices.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor of Science degree in Geology, Earth Science, Geological Engineering, or a related field
  • Ability to learn commonly used mining software
  • Minimum five (5) years’ experience in mining or exploration geology preferred.
  • Proficient geologic modeling skills required in Leapfrog Geo preferred.
  • Demonstrate a genuine ability to work cooperatively with others as part of a leadership team and encourage collaboration, trust, and transparency across the organization.
  • Forward-thinking and adaptable to dynamic situations

What We Can Offer You

  • A comprehensive compensation package including a competitive medical, dental, and vision plan with national provider networks, a 401k retirement plan with employer contribution AND employer match, paid time off, company-sponsored medical clinics, company match share purchase program, and much more!
  • Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team.
  • Endless opportunities to grow and learn with industry colleagues.
  • Access to a variety of career opportunities across the organization.
  • Nevada Gold Mines is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.

Thank you for your application, however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

description:
Fire Suppression Applications Specialist

Our trusted brands—Kidde Fire Systems, Kidde Fire Protection, and Fenwal Controls—serve industrial, commercial, marine, mission-critical, and other specialized applications. The Applications Specialist supports the design and application of Kidde Fire Systems products for commercial, industrial, mission-critical, and special-hazard applications. The role works directly with distributors, consulting engineers, Sales, Engineering, Product Management, Customer Service, and Technical Support. We are seeking an engineer with a strong technical foundation who can contribute to core design activities while developing deeper expertise in special-hazard fire suppression systems. The position emphasizes timely, accurate engineering support, clear communication, and ownership of incoming applications requests.


Specific responsibilities for this position include:


  • Review customer specifications, drawings, and project requirements to determine appropriate Kidde Fire Systems solutions.
  • Develop engineered and pre-engineered fire suppression system designs in accordance with Kidde design manuals, applicable codes and standards, and product listings/approvals.
  • Prepare and review system calculations, equipment selections, Bills of Material (BOMs), and supporting technical documentation for distributor and customer applications.
  • Perform flow calculations and system sizing and create or revise AutoCAD/Revit drawings, including layouts, piping drawings, isometrics, P&IDs, and equipment arrangements.
  • Review customer drawings and calculations and provide clear technical comments and recommendations.
  • Research technical questions and independently gather information from internal and external sources.
  • Provide applications and product support to distributors, Regional Sales Managers, consulting engineers, contractors, and other internal and external customers.
  • Support quotation and estimating activities by identifying equipment, design requirements, assumptions, and technical risks.
  • Own and manage multiple incoming applications requests from intake through completion, communicating status, priorities, technical questions, and expected delivery dates to stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with Sales, Engineering, Product Management, Customer Service, and Technical Support to resolve project-specific technical issues.
  • Support engineering standards, technical documentation, knowledge sharing, continuous improvement, customer training, and occasional field/site activities.
  • Participate in technical training and mentorship to build expertise in Kidde fire suppression technologies and progressively take on more complex engineering applications.
  • Travel occasionally to support distributor training, customer meetings, and pre-design site visits.


Required Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Fire Protection Engineering, Civil Engineering, Engineering Technology, or a related technical discipline; an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be considered.

Preferred Experience:

title: Project Manager for Comunidades Sanadoras Project
description:
Center for the Study of Hispanic Church & Community (Centro Latino)

Project Manager for Comunidades Sanadoras Project

HOURS: 30 HOURS PER WEEK

FT/PT/TEMP: TEMPORARY (TWO-YEAR TERM) FULL-TIME

EXEMPT STATUS: NON-EXEMPT

Brief Description:

Comunidades Sanadoras (Healing Communities) is a two-year formation initiative of Centro Latino designed to strengthen the resilience of Latino pastors and their families across Southern California, who are ministering amid the pressures of immigration enforcement, economic instability, and intergenerational strain. The project brings together twenty pastors and their family members in an in-person learning cohort that combines instruction, mentoring, coaching, peer learning, and practical application, supported by an online learning platform and renewal mini-grants.

The Project Manager is the operational backbone of Comunidades Sanadoras. This position is responsible for the day-to-day administration and implementation of the project for the full two-year grant period, working closely with the Director and Academic Dean of Centro Latino to ensure that recruitment, cohort gatherings, mentor coordination, mini-grant distribution, and reporting to the funder proceed smoothly and on schedule. The ideal candidate is highly organized, relationally warm, comfortable working with pastors and families navigating trauma, and able to move fluidly between administrative detail and in-person project facilitation.

Because this role supports pastors and families who are directly affected by immigration-related fear and family disruption, the Project Manager is expected to bring cultural sensitivity, discretion, and a pastoral posture to every interaction, while maintaining the administrative rigor required by a grant-funded project.

Essential Functions:

Project Operations

  • Support the recruitment and onboarding of twenty Latino pastors and their family members (one to three per pastor), as well as four mentors/coaches, in partnership with the Director and Academic Dean.
  • Coordinate the logistics of weekly small-group gatherings organized by geographic zone across Southern California, and of monthly cohort sessions that include family members.
  • Organize site visits to exemplary ministries and coordinate the participation of guest trainers and mentors, including scheduling, materials, and follow-up communication.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for participants, mentors, and partnering churches and organizations, responding to questions and troubleshooting logistics with warmth and professionalism.
  • Support participants' onboarding to the project's online learning platform and coordinate technical troubleshooting as needed.
  • Assist facilitators and mentors in preparing session materials, agendas, and reflection tools for both pastor-focused and family-inclusive sessions.
  • Attend and help facilitate in-person project activities, including occasional evening or weekend gatherings, monthly cohort meetings, and site visits.
  • Administer pre- and post-project assessment instruments and support the collection of data for the project's participatory action research process.

Administrative Management

  • Maintain accurate participant, mentor, and partner records, including attendance, communications, and project documentation.
  • Manage the application, approval, and disbursement process for the twenty participant renewal mini-grants, in coordination with OFA.
  • Track the project budget and expenses against the approved two-year grant budget, including mentor/coach stipends, site visit costs, meals, and project supplies.
  • Prepare regular progress updates and reports for Centro Latino leadership, and support the preparation of narrative and financial reports required by the funder.
  • Coordinate meeting logistics, including venue arrangements, meals for monthly cohort gatherings, materials, and technology needs.
  • Maintain the project timeline across all phases of the grant period — participant and mentor recruitment, cohort formation, and project evaluation — flagging risks to milestones as they arise.
  • Draft and send correspondence with participants, mentors, donors, and partner ministries on behalf of Centro Latino leadership.
  • Participate in weekly Centro Latino team meetings and planning/evaluation sessions.
  • Perform other project-related administrative duties as assigned by the Director or Academic Dean of Centro Latino.

Knowledge and Skills Required:

  • Fully bilingual; able to read, write, comprehend, and speak both Spanish and English fluently.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience; familiarity with Latino/a church and ministry contexts strongly preferred.
  • At least two years of experience in project or project coordination, nonprofit administration, or church/ministry operations.
  • Strong organizational and project-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple timelines and priorities across a two-year project.
  • Comfortable working with pastors and families affected by trauma, immigration-related stress, and family disruption, with sensitivity, discretion, and appropriate boundaries.
  • Effective written and verbal communicator, able to represent Centro Latino professionally with participants, mentors, donors, and community partners.
  • Technologically adept, including comfort with virtual meeting platforms, basic database or spreadsheet management, and online learning platforms.
  • Able to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and meet deadlines with minimal supervision.
  • Willingness and ability to travel locally to project sites across Southern California, including occasional evening and weekend commitments.
  • Highest level of integrity, confidentiality, and cultural humility.


Position Terms and Grant Considerations

  • This position is funded entirely through the Comunidades Sanadoras grant award and is established for a fixed term of two years, aligned with the project's approved grant period.
  • Continued employment in this role is contingent upon the continuation of grant funding; the position is expected to conclude at the end of the two-year grant term unless additional funding is secured to extend or convert the role.
  • This is a part-time position at 30 hours per week; benefits eligibility, if any, will be determined according to Fuller Theological Seminary's standard policies for employees at this level of appointment.
  • Candidates must reside in, or be willing to relocate to, the Los Angeles area, as this role requires regular in-person participation in cohort gatherings, mentor coordination, and site visits across Southern California.
  • Reports to the Director of Centro Latino, with close coordination and accountability to the Academic Dean of Centro Latino.



Additional Remarks:

  • Must be willing to abide by Fuller Theological Seminary's Community Standards.


Pay Scale:

  • Hourly rate the seminary expects to pay: $27.00 - $30.00 per hour USD


Fuller Theological Seminary is an Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. To the extent required by law, all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, or protected Veteran status. As a religious institution, Fuller Theological Seminary is permitted and reserves the right to prefer employees or prospective employees for certain positions on the basis of religion.

title: ML Compiler Engineer, Neuron Kernel Interface
description:
AWS Machine Learning accelerators are at the forefront of AWS innovation. Trainium delivers best-in-class ML training performance with the most teraflops (TFLOPS) of compute power for ML in the cloud. This is all enabled by the AWS Neuron Software Development Kit (SDK), which includes an ML compiler, the Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) compiler, and a runtime that natively integrates into popular ML frameworks such as PyTorch and JAX.

Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) is a bare-metal language and compiler for directly programming AWS Trainium instances. You can use NKI to develop, optimize, and run new operators directly on hardware while making full use of available compute and memory resources.

Explore NKI:
- https://awsdocs-neuron.readthedocs-hosted.com/en/latest/nki/index.html

AWS Neuron is used at scale by customers such as Epic Games, Snap, Airbnb, Autodesk, Amazon Alexa, and Amazon Rekognition, along with many others across a range of segments.

Amazon's Annapurna Labs is responsible for building innovative silicon and software for AWS customers. We are at the forefront of innovation, combining cloud scale with the world's most talented engineers. Our team covers multiple disciplines including silicon engineering, hardware design and verification, software, and operations. With such breadth of talent, there is opportunity to learn all the time. We operate in spaces that are very large, yet our teams remain small and agile. There is no blueprint. We're inventing. We're experimenting. When you couple that with the ability to work on so many different products and services, it makes for a unique learning culture.

Learn more about our history:
- https://www.amazon.science/how-silicon-innovation-became-the-secret-sauce-behind-awss-success

Explore the Product:
- https://aws.amazon.com/machine-learning/neuron/

As an ML Compiler Engineer with the Annapurna Neuron team, you develop and scale compilers to handle the world's largest ML workloads on AWS Trainium. You design and ship features across the compiler stack, work directly with Amazon ML partner teams to unblock their workloads, and grow your skills alongside senior engineers. You want to work close to the hardware, help bring new products and features to market, and ship high-quality code.

A background in Machine Learning, AI accelerators, or Kernel performance is helpful, but not required.

In order to be considered for this role, candidates must be located near or willing to relocate to Seattle or Cupertino.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and build compiler features for the Neuron compilers. Your work may span the frontend, intermediate representations, optimization passes, and code generation for the hardware.
- Own features from design through production: design, implement, test on hardware and simulation, and support customers.
- Work with Amazon ML teams (PyTorch, JAX, and internal model teams) to understand their workloads and unblock them.
- Give hardware teams compiler and programmability feedback on upcoming chips.
- Review code and designs, and mentor newer engineers.

A day in the life
You start the day reviewing a teammate's code for a new compiler feature, leaving feedback before it merges. Mid-morning, you work with a model team whose kernel isn't reaching peak performance on Trainium, and you trace the bottleneck through the compiler's passes. After lunch, you write and test the feature you designed last week, then run it on hardware to confirm correctness. The team moves quickly and you are always in the details.

About the team
We are the compiler teams behind AWS Neuron, the software that runs machine learning models on Amazon Trainium. Our ML compiler takes a full model from PyTorch or JAX and compiles the graph to run across the chip. The Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) is a bare-metal language and compiler that lets customers program Trainium directly, down to the compute and memory, for a new operator or a faster kernel. Together we own the path from framework model to silicon. Our mission is to make Trainium fast and fully programmable.

Our teams are small and agile, and there is opportunity to learn all the time. We work closely with the hardware, runtime and framework teams, and with the Amazon ML teams who use our compilers.

Brief Description:

Comunidades Sanadoras (Healing Communities) is a two-year formation initiative of Centro Latino designed to strengthen the resilience of Latino pastors and their families across Southern California, who are ministering amid the pressures of immigration enforcement, economic instability, and intergenerational strain. The project brings together twenty pastors and their family members in an in-person learning cohort that combines instruction, mentoring, coaching, peer learning, and practical application, supported by an online learning platform and renewal mini-grants.

The Project Manager is the operational backbone of Comunidades Sanadoras. This position is responsible for the day-to-day administration and implementation of the project for the full two-year grant period, working closely with the Director and Academic Dean of Centro Latino to ensure that recruitment, cohort gatherings, mentor coordination, mini-grant distribution, and reporting to the funder proceed smoothly and on schedule. The ideal candidate is highly organized, relationally warm, comfortable working with pastors and families navigating trauma, and able to move fluidly between administrative detail and in-person project facilitation.

Because this role supports pastors and families who are directly affected by immigration-related fear and family disruption, the Project Manager is expected to bring cultural sensitivity, discretion, and a pastoral posture to every interaction, while maintaining the administrative rigor required by a grant-funded project.

Essential Functions:

Project Operations

  • Support the recruitment and onboarding of twenty Latino pastors and their family members (one to three per pastor), as well as four mentors/coaches, in partnership with the Director and Academic Dean.
  • Coordinate the logistics of weekly small-group gatherings organized by geographic zone across Southern California, and of monthly cohort sessions that include family members.
  • Organize site visits to exemplary ministries and coordinate the participation of guest trainers and mentors, including scheduling, materials, and follow-up communication.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for participants, mentors, and partnering churches and organizations, responding to questions and troubleshooting logistics with warmth and professionalism.
  • Support participants' onboarding to the project's online learning platform and coordinate technical troubleshooting as needed.
  • Assist facilitators and mentors in preparing session materials, agendas, and reflection tools for both pastor-focused and family-inclusive sessions.
  • Attend and help facilitate in-person project activities, including occasional evening or weekend gatherings, monthly cohort meetings, and site visits.
  • Administer pre- and post-project assessment instruments and support the collection of data for the project's participatory action research process.

Administrative Management

  • Maintain accurate participant, mentor, and partner records, including attendance, communications, and project documentation.
  • Manage the application, approval, and disbursement process for the twenty participant renewal mini-grants, in coordination with OFA.
  • Track the project budget and expenses against the approved two-year grant budget, including mentor/coach stipends, site visit costs, meals, and project supplies.
  • Prepare regular progress updates and reports for Centro Latino leadership, and support the preparation of narrative and financial reports required by the funder.
  • Coordinate meeting logistics, including venue arrangements, meals for monthly cohort gatherings, materials, and technology needs.
  • Maintain the project timeline across all phases of the grant period — participant and mentor recruitment, cohort formation, and project evaluation — flagging risks to milestones as they arise.
  • Draft and send correspondence with participants, mentors, donors, and partner ministries on behalf of Centro Latino leadership.
  • Participate in weekly Centro Latino team meetings and planning/evaluation sessions.
  • Perform other project-related administrative duties as assigned by the Director or Academic Dean of Centro Latino.

Knowledge and Skills Required:

  • Fully bilingual; able to read, write, comprehend, and speak both Spanish and English fluently.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience; familiarity with Latino/a church and ministry contexts strongly preferred.
  • At least two years of experience in project or project coordination, nonprofit administration, or church/ministry operations.
  • Strong organizational and project-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple timelines and priorities across a two-year project.
  • Comfortable working with pastors and families affected by trauma, immigration-related stress, and family disruption, with sensitivity, discretion, and appropriate boundaries.
  • Effective written and verbal communicator, able to represent Centro Latino professionally with participants, mentors, donors, and community partners.
  • Technologically adept, including comfort with virtual meeting platforms, basic database or spreadsheet management, and online learning platforms.
  • Able to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and meet deadlines with minimal supervision.
  • Willingness and ability to travel locally to project sites across Southern California, including occasional evening and weekend commitments.
  • Highest level of integrity, confidentiality, and cultural humility.


Position Terms and Grant Considerations

  • This position is funded entirely through the Comunidades Sanadoras grant award and is established for a fixed term of two years, aligned with the project's approved grant period.
  • Continued employment in this role is contingent upon the continuation of grant funding; the position is expected to conclude at the end of the two-year grant term unless additional funding is secured to extend or convert the role.
  • This is a part-time position at 30 hours per week; benefits eligibility, if any, will be determined according to Fuller Theological Seminary's standard policies for employees at this level of appointment.
  • Candidates must reside in, or be willing to relocate to, the Los Angeles area, as this role requires regular in-person participation in cohort gatherings, mentor coordination, and site visits across Southern California.
  • Reports to the Director of Centro Latino, with close coordination and accountability to the Academic Dean of Centro Latino.



Additional Remarks:

  • Must be willing to abide by Fuller Theological Seminary's Community Standards.


Pay Scale:

  • Hourly rate the seminary expects to pay: $27.00 - $30.00 per hour USD


Fuller Theological Seminary is an Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. To the extent required by law, all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, or protected Veteran status. As a religious institution, Fuller Theological Seminary is permitted and reserves the right to prefer employees or prospective employees for certain positions on the basis of religion.

title: Director, HR Service Center
description:
Job Description

The Director, HR Service Center provides leadership and strategic oversight for the HR Service Center, ensuring efficient, accurate, and consistent delivery of HR services across the organization. This includes ensuring the HR Service Center functions are cost-efficient while maintaining high productivity and consistent service quality. Manages daily activities, optimizes processes, and enhances the employee experience by ensuring high-quality service delivery, while align budgetary targets to production. The Director collaborates with HR leadership, business units, and key stakeholders to align HR support services with organizational goals and business needs.

  • Provides leadership and oversight for the HR Service Center to maintain low cost and efficient delivery of HR services to employees, leaders, and other stakeholders. Partners with HR and organizational leaders to align service delivery with organizational goals and priorities, while maintaining a focus on cost effectiveness, service quality, consistency, and employee experience.
  • Oversees the development and execution of operational strategies for the HR Service Center by identifying opportunities for process improvements and efficiencies. Performs data and process analysis to enhance service delivery and implements plans that ensure the Service Center meets the evolving HR support needs of the organization.
  • Provides strategic oversight to ensure uninterrupted, timely delivery of functional services across the organization by leveraging dashboards and analytics. Utilizes data-driven insights to forecast workload trends and proactively align resources for optimal performance.
  • Builds and maintains strong partnerships with HR Lines of Business, Centers of Excellence, and employee groups. Collaborates with leaders across the organization to implement HR service center processes and solutions that support business goals and comply with HR policies as well as local, state, and federal regulations.
  • Oversees the day-to-day delivery of HR Service Center functions to ensure consistent, accurate, and timely support for employees and leaders across the organization.
  • Manages special projects by clarifying priorities, coordinating requirements, and ensuring timely completion of deliverables. Oversees the department’s budget and expenses, while also supervising the development and use of metrics that support forecasting, operational insights, and continuous improvement.
  • Leads and develops the HR Service Center team by overseeing recruiting, training, coaching, and performance management. Supports staff development through skill assessments and growth plans to ensure the team is equipped to meet service and organizational objectives.
  • Supports change management initiatives by helping to plan and implement process and organizational changes with a focus on employee experience, stakeholder impact, and operational integrity.
  • Manages vendor relationships, monitors service delivery, and stays informed of vendor plans to assess potential impacts on current operations and future HR Service Center functionality.

  • Bachelor's Degree Business administration, human resources, or a related field - minimum
  • Master's Degree Business administration, human resources, or a related field - preferred

Experience
  • 8 years HR shared services, HR, Payroll, Finance or other related shared services experience - minimum
  • 4 years Leadership in Shared Services or related leadership experience - minimum

Licenses and Certifications
  • No license or certification required

### Description

**IMPORTANT APPLICATION INFORMATION**

Information Technology (IT) currently has an opening which will be filled at either the Project Manager or Senior Project Manager level.  As you complete your application, please be sure to include all applicable information (completed degrees, related work history, etc.) so you can be considered for the appropriate level.

Offering salary may be made above the minimum of the posted salary range up through the midpoint, depending upon qualifications, experience, education, certifications, training, and internal equity considerations.

_This job classification description is intended to be generic in nature and not an exhaustive list of all duties and responsibilities.  The specific tasks/duties may vary based on position assignment and as determined by the Town of Queen Creek._

**IMPORTANT DATES**

- **This recruitment closes October 25th.**
- **First round of interviews are anticipated to take place the week of November 1.**
- **Expected start date is November 2026 for the successful candidate.**

**IT Project Manager ($93,564.96 - $135,669.31 Annually)**

Positions assigned to this class are responsible for planning, coordinating and managing IT related projects from inception through timely implementation/roll-outs and support. Incumbents have extensive knowledge of complex systems and/or applications and their interactions.

This is a fully qualified and experienced level professional classification in the information technology job family. Incumbents perform the full range of duties that requires extensive and broad knowledge and skill within an assigned IT functional area.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES**

_The following are intended to describe core work functions of this classification. While the level and broad nature of essential duties may not change, specific work tasks will vary over time depending on the Town’s needs._

- Implements IT strategies that deliver projects on schedule and within budget;
- Manages IT related projects from inception to completion; researches assigned problems or issues, analyzes findings, develops reports and recommendations, and presents findings to relevant staff; facilitates meetings with staff and contractors to discuss project goals and progress.
- Plans complex projects by developing and writing scope of work and all other project documentation; determines the appropriate use of professional/technical staff and resources to conduct projects; communicates and coordinates regularly with appropriate personnel as it relates to projects in order to maximize the effectiveness and efficiency of interdepartmental operations and activities.
- Assists in long range and strategic technology planning; develops and executes technology life cycle management strategy; identifies plans and implements technology projects; develops technology project proposals, including business justification and risk assessment for projects; assigns professional and technical staff and resources to conduct the projects.
- Creates reports for managing work and data.
- Participate in training staff on use of application and new features.
- Performs related work as assigned.

**IT Project Manager, Senior ($107,122.66 - $155,327.84 Annually)**

Positions assigned to this class are responsible for managing the most complex and highest-dollar-value projects in an area specific to the type of project managed. This includes responsibilities such as securing grants/funding, fiscal management, team coordination, and public involvement. In the Information Technology Department, this also includes providing technology leadership by establishing project management/governance standards, processes, and policies.

This role oversees all project efforts, budgets, and major initiatives. It supports and helps define project templates, success metrics, resource allocation, and reporting practices. The position serves as a mentor and project management resource for all IT staff and leads the Project Management Office (PMO) function.

This is a senior-level professional classification in the Information Technology job family. Incumbents perform the full range of advanced duties that demonstrate broad, practical knowledge in a variety of IT project and program management processes, methods, techniques, and best practices.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES**

_The following are intended to describe core work functions of this classification.  While the level and broad nature of essential duties may not change, specific work tasks will vary over time depending on the Town’s needs._

- Lead, organize, and direct cross-functional project teams to ensure strategic IT projects are delivered on time, within scope, and on budget.
- Oversee the delivery of the Project Management Office (PMO) function, including data management, schedule management, risk and issue tracking, program reporting, and administrative oversight.
- Manage and effectively utilize an enterprise project management tool for resource allocation, planning, and project status/metrics reporting across the IT Department.
- Maintain regular communication with IT leadership regarding project status, risks, dependencies, and strategic needs.
- Manage vendor relationships, ensure compliance with contracts, and identify opportunities to improve vendor efficiency and performance.
- Set performance goals for project team members and support their development through coaching, evaluations, and ongoing training.
- Oversee the maintenance of IT project tracking systems and portfolio management tools (e.g., TeamDynamix) to ensure accurate documentation and reporting of initiatives.
- Guide the development and implementation of documentation standards, including knowledge base articles, process documentation, and configuration guides.
- Drive continuous process improvement efforts aimed at increasing operational efficiency, scalability, and alignment with ITIL and project management best practices.
- Remain current on technical trends and provide recommendations to management on new project methodologies.
- Support project estimation, risk assessment, and milestone management.
- Assist with policy and procedure development related to project management.
- Prepare and deliver project performance reports, risk assessments, and executive summaries to senior leadership.
- Provide effective leadership, mentoring, and training within areas of responsibility and expertise.
- Build strong team relationships to accomplish goals collaboratively.
- Document and maintain all processes, guidelines, and procedures.
- Perform related work as assigned.

### Typical Qualifications

**IT Project Manager**

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS** (at job entry)

**Education and Experience:**

Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited college or university in computer science, information systems, or a related field and 3 years of experience in implementation of IT infrastructure, system integration and/or software applications; or an equivalent combination of directly related education and experience.

**Special Requirements**:

To be eligible, incumbents cannot be on the Office of Inspector General (OIG) list of Excluded Individuals/Entities (LEIE).

**LICENSING/CERTIFICATION REQUIREMENTS**

- AZ Driver’s License.
- Project Management Certification (PMP) within one (1) year of hire.
- Maintain all certifications/licenses required at job entry.
- May require PD background check.

**IT Project Manager, Senior**

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS** (at job entry)

**Education and Experience:**

Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited college or university in computer science, information systems, or a related field. Master’s degree preferred. Six (6) years of progressively responsible experience in IT project management is required. An equivalent combination of directly related education and experience may be considered.

**Special Requirements:**

To be eligible, incumbents cannot be on the Office of Inspector General (OIG) list of Excluded Individuals/Entities (LEIE).

**LICENSING/CERTIFICATION REQUIREMENTS**

- Valid driver’s license.
- PMP, PMI-ACP, PgMP, or equivalent project management certification required.
- Maintain all certifications and licenses required at job entry.

title: Data engineer
description:
The Data Engineer is responsible for building, supporting, and optimising scalable, repeatable, and secure data pipelines and analytical platforms. Operating as a core member of an agile engineering team, the role focuses on enabling business insights through the integration, transformation, and management of large-scale batch and real-time data solutions. The Data Engineer works across cloud and big data technologies to architect, develop, and support modern data platforms that enable analytics, reporting, automation, and data-driven decision-making.

Key Responsibilities Design, build, and maintain scalable data analytics frameworks and data platforms. Translate complex functional and technical requirements into scalable architecture and high-performing data solutions. Develop and support batch and real-time data processing solutions using modern big data technologies. Create and maintain secure and reliable data pipelines between on-premise systems and AWS cloud environments. Develop and maintain ETL processes and data transformation workflows using Talend or similar ETL tools. Manipulate, process, and analyse data using Python and related technologies. Develop and support Big Data and Business Intelligence solutions including automated testing and deployment practices. Process large-scale datasets using Hadoop paradigms and AWS EMR services. Support production data feeds and resolve operational issues through break-fix support activities. Contribute to database development, optimisation, and operational management. Participate in software development, Dev Ops, and data operations activities. Ensure alignment with policies, standards, procedures, business continuity, and disaster recovery practices. Research and evaluate emerging technologies, tools, and frameworks relevant to data engineering and analytics. Collaborate with business and technical stakeholders to understand data requirements and deliver effective solutions. Essential Skills & Experience 5+ years’ experience in Data Engineering or Software Engineering roles. 2+ years’ experience working with Big Data technologies and platforms. 2+ years’ experience with ETL processes and tooling. 2+ years’ experience working with AWS cloud technologies. Strong experience with Python for data manipulation and processing. Hands-on experience with AWS services including EMR, EC2, and S3. Experience with Py Spark, Spark, Hadoop, or distributed data processing frameworks. Strong understanding of data modelling, data structures, and scalable data architecture design. Experience designing highly scalable distributed systems using open-source technologies. Strong understanding of object-oriented design, coding standards, and testing practices. Experience working with large-scale data infrastructure and analytical platforms. Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills. Desirable Skills & Experience Experience with real-time streaming and event-driven data processing. Exposure to cloud-native data engineering architectures. Experience implementing automated deployment and CI/CD practices for data platforms. Exposure to business intelligence and analytics tooling. Experience working within agile software delivery environments. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, or equivalent practical experience. AWS certification would be advantageous. Behavioural Competencies Strong analytical and problem-solving mindset. Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills. Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality. Ability to work effectively both independently and within collaborative agile teams. Adaptability and willingness to learn evolving technologies and tools. Proactive mindset with focus on innovation and continuous improvement. What We Offer Competitive salary and benefits package. Opportunity to work on modern cloud and big data platforms. Exposure to large-scale data engineering and analytics projects. Collaborative and innovative engineering environment. Professional growth and learning opportunities. Opportunity to contribute to impactful data-driven solutions.

Our employees are unified in a shared dedication to our customers’ mission and quest for professional growth. L3Harris provides an inclusive, engaging environment designed to empower employees and promote work-life success. Fundamental to our culture is an unwavering focus on values, dedication to our communities, and commitment to excellence in everything we do.

L3Harris is the Trusted Disruptor in defense tech. With customers’ mission-critical needs always in mind, our employees deliver end-to-end technology solutions connecting the space, air, land, sea and cyber domains in the interest of national security.

**Job Title: Lead, Software Engineer/Front-End**

**Job Code: 46216**

**Job Location: Melbourne, FL (Patrick Space Force Base)**

**Job Schedule: 9/80: Employees work 9 out of every 14 days – totaling 80 hours worked – and have every other Friday off**

**Job Description:**

We are seeking highly skilled and motivated Lead Software/Integration Engineer with experience in modern front-end development, Javascript, AWS, Docker, Linux, CI/CD, and AI-assisted development to support front-end modernization, software integration, and mission-system reliability improvements. The ideal candidate will provide technical leadership across software and infrastructure teams and work onsite at Patrick Space Force Base.

**Essential Functions:**

- Build modern, responsive, intuitive front-end solutions using current web frameworks and best practices.
- Apply software engineering best practices across the full development lifecycle, including code reviews, automated testing, version control, and CI/CD pipelines.

- Deploy and maintain applications in AWS, ensuring scalability, security, resilience, and cost-effectiveness.
- Support containerized deployments using Docker and, where applicable, Kubernetes.
- Engage with customers daily to refine requirements and improve application functionality.
- Prepare and brief technical designs, implementation plans, roadmaps, and documentation.
- Produce and maintain technical documentation for system design, application architecture, deployment procedures, and sustainment activities.
- Familiarity with databases such as PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, DynamoDB, or other relational/non-relational data stores.
- Knowledge of infrastructure as code tools such as Terraform, CloudFormation, or similar.
- Security+ Certification or any DoD IAT Level II Certification, or ability to obtain certification within 6 months of accepting position.

**Qualifications:**

- Bachelor’s degree in computer science or computer engineering and a minimum of 9 years of prior relevant experience. Graduate Degree and a minimum of 7 years of prior related experience. In lieu of a degree, minimum of 13 years of prior related experience.
- Active TS clearance with the ability to obtain SCI.

**Preferred Additional Skills:**

- Experience developing AI/ML-enabled mission applications, analytical tools, or decision-support capabilities involving advanced data processing, automation, visualization, and user interaction.
- Experience developing and deploying applications in Amazon Web Services (AWS).
- Proficiency with front-end technologies such as React, Angular, Vue, JavaScript/TypeScript, HTML, and CSS.
- Experience with Docker, CI/CD, Git, REST APIs, microservices, and secure software development.
- Experience with scientific, sensor-derived, geophysical, acoustic, seismic, infrasonic, or other mission-relevant technical data is highly desired.
- Experience building back-end services and APIs using Python, Java, Node.js, .NET, or similar.
- Experience with AI-assisted development tools
- Experience transitioning research or prototype capabilities into operational software tools, supporting classified DoD mission environments strongly preferred.
- Experience supporting Agile software development teams and participating in Scrum ceremonies.
- Experience building and deploying mission applications in classified or high-security environments.
- Familiarity with the C2S Access Portal (CAP) and high-side AWS environments is highly desired.
- Experience with containerization and orchestration technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes.

Skills:

Organizational skills help manage multiple units simultaneously, track progress, and maintain detailed records. Problem-solving abilities are frequently applied to address unexpected maintenance issues or tenant concerns promptly. Additionally, proficiency with relevant software tools enhances efficiency in managing work orders and inventory.

title: Senior DevOps Engineer
description:
Position Overview:


We are seeking a highly skilled Senior Multi-Cloud DevOps Engineer with extensive experience managing workloads across Azure, AWS, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP). In this role, you will focus on architecting and scaling containerized infrastructures using Kubernetes, driving automation via Infrastructure as Code (Terraform), and building robust, automated pipelines. Having a background or familiarity with .NET application deployments is a strong plus.



Key Responsibilities:



  • Multi-Cloud Administration: Manage, secure, and scale cloud infrastructure across Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services (AWS), and Google Cloud Platform (GCP).


  • GitOps Automation: Design, build, and maintain GitOps-driven workflows using Flux (v2) or Argo CD to automate deployments across AKS, EKS, and GKE clusters.


  • Kubernetes Orchestration: Administer and optimize managed Kubernetes environments (AKS, EKS, GKE), ensuring high availability, strict security compliance, and cost-efficiency.


  • CI/CD Engineering: Design and manage scalable, secure CI/CD pipelines using Azure DevOps Pipelines and GitHub Actions.


  • Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Automate end-to-end multi-cloud infrastructure provisioning using advanced modular Terraform.


  • Observability & Monitoring: Implement enterprise-level observability and logging strategies using tools like Prometheus, Grafana, ELK, Azure Monitor, or GCP Operations Suite.


  • Developer Collaboration: Partner with development teams (specifically working on .NET environments) to optimize containerization strategies (Docker, Helm) and define zero-downtime release models.




Requirements:



  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in DevOps, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), or Cloud Infrastructure roles.


  • True Multi-Cloud Expertise: Proven experience operating and architecting environments simultaneously in Azure, AWS, and GCP.


  • Deep Kubernetes Knowledge: Hands-on experience administering production-grade clusters (AKS, EKS, or GKE), implementing HPA, Cluster Autoscaler, and fine-tuning resource constraints.


  • GitOps Mastery: Solid, practical understanding of GitOps principles, specifically using Flux or Argo CD combined with Helm or Kustomize.


  • IaC Proficiency: Advanced skills in Terraform, including state management, locking strategies, and writing reusable multi-provider modules.


  • Pipeline Security: Experience securing CI/CD pipelines (Azure DevOps / GitHub Actions) utilizing managed identities, secrets managers, and vulnerability scanning tools.


  • Language Proficiency: Advanced/Fluent English communication skills (written and spoken) to collaborate daily with US-based stakeholders.




Nice to Have / Pluses:



  • Background or experience supporting, containerizing, and deploying .NET Core / .NET 6+ applications.


  • Scripting expertise in Python, Bash, or PowerShell for advanced automation tasks.




Tools & Technologies:



  • Cloud Platforms: Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services (AWS), Google Cloud Platform (GCP).


  • Containerization & Orchestration: Docker, Kubernetes (AKS, EKS, GKE).


  • GitOps & Packaging: Flux (v2), Helm, Kustomize, Argo CD.


  • CI/CD: Azure DevOps Pipelines, GitHub Actions.


  • Infrastructure as Code: Terraform.


  • Monitoring & Observability: Prometheus, Grafana, ELK, Cloud-native monitoring suites.


  • Version Control: Git, GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket.

title: Clinic Director
description:
Why work at Greenwich House?

At Greenwich House, we believe in empowering communities through transformative programs, we offer more than a job – we offer a mission. When you work with us, you become part of a passionate, collaborative team committed to making a difference in people’s lives. Every initiative, class, and outreach effort we deliver is fueled by a shared commitment to equity and compassion.


Founded in 1902 as a settlement house aimed at supporting New York City's growing immigrant population, Greenwich House has since evolved into a dynamic nonprofit organization dedicated to fostering wellness, creativity, and connection across the city. Today, Greenwich House offers a diverse range of programs in health, human services, education, and the arts, serving thousands of New Yorkers each year. Learn more at www.greenwichhouse.org.


The Opportunity

The Center for Resiliency & Wellness Clinic Director is a transformational leader responsible for driving a high-performing, trauma-informed outpatient mental health clinic that prioritizes trust, accountability, innovation, and exceptional patient experience. This leader ensures the clinic operates on a strong growth trajectory while cultivating a team of highly qualified, compassionate professionals who are committed to clinical excellence and open to innovative approaches to care.


The Clinic Director will oversee daily operations of an Article 31 Mental Health Outpatient Treatment and Rehabilitative Services Program, while actively shaping a culture that balances clinical integrity, operational discipline, staff accountability, and forward-thinking practices such as clay therapy, play-based interventions, and modernized recruitment strategies (e.g., Zocdoc and other access points).


This role goes beyond traditional community-based clinic management. The Clinic Director is responsible for redefining expectations of care delivery - ensuring that every patient experiences a welcoming, dignified, and thoughtfully designed environment, supported by responsive customer service and a team deeply invested in patient success.



Responsibilities

  • Build and sustain a culture of trust, accountability, and high performance. Model trauma-informed, patient-centered, and recovery-oriented care; recruit, develop, and retain a balanced team of clinicians and support staff; and promote a shift from minimum standards to exceptional care delivery.
  • Drive clinic growth through innovative programming, strong referral pipelines, and modern access strategies (e.g., Zocdoc, community partnerships). Expand services while maintaining quality and compliance, and integrate creative, evidence-informed approaches such as expressive therapies (e.g., clay therapy), play-based spaces, and afterschool transition supports.
  • Ensure a bright, welcoming, and professionally maintained environment that reflects dignity and respect. Set and uphold high standards for customer service, responsiveness, and patient engagement across all interactions.
  • Oversee daily operations, staffing, and workflows to ensure efficiency, coverage, and high-quality service delivery. Maintain accountability for productivity benchmarks, KPIs, and financial performance, and ensure compliance with OMH, NYS, and Federal regulations, including audit readiness and corrective actions.
  • Maintain a small caseload while providing leadership on complex cases. Ensure high-quality documentation, supervision, and adherence to best practices, supporting care for diverse populations with trauma histories, co-occurring disorders, and complex needs.
  • Provide structured, meaningful supervision and invest in staff development through training in innovative, evidence-based, and brief intervention models. Foster a culture of continuous learning, collaboration, and shared accountability.
  • Partner with the Vice President of Behavioral Health Services and collaborate with admissions, care coordination, and external partners to ensure seamless patient flow and continuity of care. Represent the clinic in internal and external forums to reinforce its reputation for innovation and excellence.



What You’ll Bring

  • Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW), LMSW, LMHC, plus four (4) years of clinical experience; supervisory experience strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience building and leading high-performing teams grounded in trust and accountability.
  • Strong commitment to trauma-informed care and innovative clinical practices.
  • Experience with or openness to non-traditional and creative therapeutic modalities (e.g., play therapy, expressive therapies).
  • Proven ability to drive program growth while maintaining quality and staff engagement.
  • Excellent communication, leadership presence, and decision-making skills.
  • Deep understanding of clinical documentation, compliance, and regulatory standards.
  • Ability to shift organizational mindset toward elevated care standards and patient experience.
  • Experience working across diverse populations and age groups.



Employment Details

  • Department: Health Services Division - Center for Resiliency & Wellness
  • Location: Onsite - 623 Broadway, New York, NY 10012
  • Schedule: Monday - Friday; 35 hours/week; 9:00am-5:00pm and 11:00am-7:00pm (rotating hours)

  • Reports To: Vice President of Behavioral Health Services

Salary Range
